## CPython 3.13 Free Threading and Extension Imports

CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading as a configuration in which the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) can be disabled. In that configuration, an application’s runtime choice also affects what happens when it imports an extension.

If an extension does not explicitly declare support for free threading, importing it produces a warning and enables the GIL. The declaration mechanism differs depending on whether the extension uses multi-phase or single-phase initialization.

Declaring support signals compatibility with the free-threading runtime mode; it does not establish that the extension’s code is thread-safe. Making the code thread-safe is a separate responsibility for extension authors.
